stages.source_citation: 31 CFR 1010.100(xx) (definition of "structure (structuring)")
stages.source_quote: "...to conduct one or more transactions in currency, in any amount, at one or more financial institutions, on one or more days, in any manner, for the purpose of evading the reporting requirements... The transaction or transactions need not exceed the $10,000 reporting threshold at any single financial institution on any single day in order to constitute structuring within the meaning of this definition."
stages.note: AMOUNT is grounded (override $8,200-$9,900 sits under the $10,000 CTR threshold of 31 CFR 1010.311 — cite Q['ctr']). RATE is not. IMPORTANT: the finance.yaml `ctr_structuring_window` constraint (k:4, floor:$7,000, window 7d) is presented as '31 CFR 1010.311' but NEITHER the count-of-4, the 7-day window, NOR the $7,000 floor appears in the CFR. The premise that this yields a grounded 0.57 deposits/day is FALSE. Recommend k=1 (neutral default) and re-label the constraint's k/floor/window as a modelling choice.

stages.assumption: One approve per victim (ERC-20 allowance is multi-use); victims = 8-40; stage window = 1-7 days => 8/7=1.14/day to 40/1=40/day. This bounds the COUNT the mechanism requires; it is not a rate the standard states.
stages.source_citation: ERC-20 Token Standard, `approve` (EIP-20)
stages.source_quote: "Allows `_spender` to withdraw from your account multiple times, up to the `_value` amount. If this function is called again it overwrites the current allowance with `_value`."
stages.note: DERIVABLE from mechanism, not from a stated rate. ERC-20 `approve` grants multi-use spend rights in ONE call, so the campaign needs exactly 1 approve per victim (2 if the spec's set-to-0-first note is honoured). ASSUMPTION: each victim approves once over the stage window.

stages.source_citation: CAPEC — TCP SYN / port scanning
stages.source_quote: "Unlike TCP Connect scanning, it is possible to scan thousands of ports per second using this method"
stages.note: Modelling choice, not grounded. CAPEC states a CAPABILITY CEILING ('thousands of ports per second'), not a campaign rate; using it as the rate would give ~10^8/day. MITRE T1046 states no rate. The current 100-800/day encodes a 'low-and-slow' choice. Recommend k=1 unless a scan-rate source is added.

stages.source_citation: CAPEC-49 Password Brute Forcing
stages.source_quote: "an adversary can brute force this password in maximum 1+26+26^2+26^3+26^4+26^5 = ... = 12,356,631 attempts, and half these tries (6,178,316) on average"
stages.note: Modelling choice, not grounded. CAPEC-49 gives an exhaustive-search COUNT (6.18M attempts on average), which is a search-space size, not a rate — using it would give ~10^7/day. ATT&CK T1110.003 says spraying stays 'under lockout' but names no threshold. The natural grounding source (NIST SP 800-63B throttling guidance, <=100 failed attempts) is NOT in the corpus — CORPUS GAP. Recommend k=1 pending that source.
Modelling choice, not grounded. MITRE T1021 is a prose technique description; ATT&CK states no rates anywhere (grep for 'interval'/'frequenc'/'sleep' returns only qualitative prose). Recommend k=1.

stages.source_citation: MITRE ATT&CK T1071 / T1568 (DNS beaconing)
stages.source_quote: "DNS beacons may be difficult to detect because the beacons infrequently communicate with infected devices." (qualitative only; no interval stated)
stages.note: Modelling choice, not grounded. ATT&CK T1071/T1568 say beaconing is 'periodic'/'infrequent' but state no interval. NIST SP 800-94's 'every 15 minutes, every 30 minutes' span is about NBA FLOW-BATCH COLLECTION LATENCY, not beacon cadence — do NOT cite it here. The YAML's '~hourly to ~15-min beacons' comment is an unsourced choice. Recommend k=1.
Modelling choice, not grounded. MITRE T1041/T1029 describe scheduling ('at certain times of day or at certain intervals') without numbers. Recommend k=1.

stages.source_citation: CMS NCCI Medically Unlikely Edits — Practitioner Services (MUE table, eff. 07-01-2026)
stages.source_quote: "HCPCS/CPT Code | Practitioner Services MUE Values | MUE Adjudication Indicator | MUE Rationale | 0001U | 1 | 2 Date of Service Edit: Policy | ..." (per-code max units of service per beneficiary per date of service)
stages.note: Modelling choice for RATE, not grounded. Upcoding does not change claim VOLUME at all — it changes the code on claims the provider already files. The corpus grounds the ATTRIBUTE (HCPCS/CPT code set), never the rate. NCCI MUE caps units per code per beneficiary per date of service; it says nothing about claims/day. Recommend k=1 — which here is not merely a default but SEMANTICALLY CORRECT: an upcoder bills at a normal cadence by construction.

stages.source_citation: CMS NCCI Medically Unlikely Edits — Practitioner Services (MUE table, eff. 07-01-2026)
stages.source_quote: "HCPCS/CPT Code | Practitioner Services MUE Values | MUE Adjudication Indicator | MUE Rationale | 0001U | 1 | 2 Date of Service Edit: Policy | ..." (per-code max units of service per beneficiary per date of service)
stages.note: Modelling choice, not grounded. NCCI MUE is a per-code/per-beneficiary/per-date-of-service UNITS cap — it is a genuine count-in-a-window, but it constrains the `units` field, NOT a provider's claims/day. No corpus source states an implausible-daily-claim-volume threshold. The 150-400/day is unsourced. Recommend k=1 unless a per-provider volume source (e.g. CMS Provider Utilization & Payment PUF) is added — CORPUS GAP.

stages.source_citation: CMS NCCI Medically Unlikely Edits — Practitioner Services (MUE table, eff. 07-01-2026)
stages.source_quote: "HCPCS/CPT Code | Practitioner Services MUE Values | MUE Adjudication Indicator | MUE Rationale | 0001U | 1 | 2 Date of Service Edit: Policy | ..." (per-code max units of service per beneficiary per date of service)
stages.note: RATE is a modelling choice; the ATTRIBUTE is grounded. NCCI PTP edits (4,041 chunks) ground WHICH Column1/Column2 code pairs may not be billed together, and NCCI MUE grounds the max units per code per beneficiary per DOS — so the `units` override IS citable (A-grade for the attribute). Neither states claims/day. Like upcoding, unbundling does not change cadence by construction: recommend k=1.

Modelling choice, not grounded — BUT THIS IS THE BEST CORPUS-GAP CANDIDATE IN THE WHOLE RULE BASE. CMS's Part D Overutilization Monitoring System (OMS) publishes an explicit count-in-a-window criterion for opioid doctor/pharmacy shopping (beneficiaries meeting an MME threshold with >=N prescribers and >=M pharmacies over a lookback). That source is NOT in the corpus. Fetching the CMS OMS / Part D Opioid Overutilization guidance would make this stage a genuine (A) and would also ground `ring_size` (distinct prescribers). Until then: recommend k=1, labelled a modelling choice.
